text:
andrea: FYI alert - eu-west dedicated pool reporting ~75% of GPUs disconnected, queue length for dedicated jobs jumped 4x. seeing increased 503s to customers in eu-west.
andrea: grafana: https://graf.redwood/g/abcd1234/cluster-eu-west - error spikes on /v1/generate + node disconnect logs.
sre-bot: [ALERT] cluster.eu-west.dedicated.pool_down threshold breached (75% nodes down) at 2026-03-18T09:41:18Z :rotating_light:
sam_oncall: taking this. are we confident it's a node/network boundary issue and not control-plane causing evictions?
andrea: looks like NIC flapping in az-2. kube logs show repeated cni plugin restarts and kubelet disconnects. sample log:
```
Mar 18 09:35:08 node-az2 kubelet[...]: NetworkPlugin cni failed: error listing interfaces: RPC timed out
Mar 18 09:35:09 node-az2 kubelet[...]: NodeStatus -> NotReady
```
mike: confirming from infra side - cloud provider shows transient fabric errors in eu-west-2 az-2. support ticket open with provider. ETA unknown.
sam_oncall: plan: 1) shift non-reserved traffic off dedicated -> hosted in increments 25% 2) start warm replacement nodes in another AZ (eu-west-2 az-1) 3) throttle background/batch orgs if needed. i'll execute step 1 now.
sam_oncall: running routing command to reduce dedicated weight for eu-west to 0.6
sam_oncall: `routectl set-weight --region eu-west --pool dedicated --weight 0.6 --reason "az-2 flapping"`
deploy-bot: rollout started: traffic-policy/eu-west v2 -> adjusting weights
sam_oncall: routectl response: OK updated weights. new routing: dedicated=0.6 hosted=0.4
andrea: note: shifting to hosted will cold-start KV caches for some hot prefixes — expect transient 50-200ms latency spikes on first requests. we should warm top 10 org prefixes after shift.
eva: cost question — how long do we expect to stay on hosted? can we triage by org to avoid cost for large reserved customers?
sam_oncall: initial plan is to keep shift until provider marks fabric healthy or new nodes join (estimated node reprovision 10-15m). we'll prioritize reserved orgs to stay on dedicated where possible.
mike: I've started replacement nodes in az-1, cloud request sent. provisioning logs show jobs queued; ETA ~12m.
andrea: warming caches for top prefixes now: `curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/internal/warm-cache -d '{"prefixes":["orgA","orgB","orgC"]}'`
sam_oncall: warming ok. also enabling soft-throttle for batch orgs: `quotactl set-priority --region eu-west --priority batch --limit 0.3`
sre-bot: [INFO] traffic-shift applied. observed dedicated queue length dropping.
andrea: metrics: 503s down from 3.2% -> 0.9% in the last 2m; p95 latency bumped from 120ms -> 210ms for warmed prefixes initially.
sam_oncall: good. will keep monitoring and only escalate to broad throttles if trend reverses.
eva: pls capture cost delta for the hosted bump — we might want to authorize an emergency spend threshold for this event.
mike: provider updated ticket: fabric issue detected, mitigation in progress. they expect <30m to full stabilization.
sam_oncall: tentative timeline: stay on partial hosted (40%) for now, continue node reprovision, revisit in 20m. action items: - sam: continue monitoring + finish node reprovision - andrea: post simple runbook note about cache warmers + expected latency - mike: follow up provider ticket and update ETA - eva: estimate immediate cost impact and notify finance if >$X
deploy-bot: traffic-policy/eu-west v2 -> completed (stable)
andrea: thanks everyone. leaving alert channel open. will kick off incident doc after we confirm provider fix.
mike: will post provider incident update when available :thumbsup:
sre-bot: [RESOLVED?] cluster.eu-west.dedicated.pool_down reduced below threshold at 2026-03-18T09:53:40Z (recovering)
sam_oncall: marking this thread monitored. will convert to postmortem later.
